title: Chain of Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

claims.statement: Generating a chain of thought improves the ability of large language models to perform complex reasoning.
claims.evidence: Experiments on three large language models show that chain of thought prompting improves performance on a range of arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks.

claims.statement: Chain of thought reasoning abilities emerge naturally in sufficiently large language models via chain of thought prompting.
claims.evidence: In particular, we show how such reasoning abilities emerge naturally in sufficiently large language models via a simple method called chain of thought prompting, where a few chain of thought demonstrations are provided as exemplars in prompting.

claims.statement: Prompting a 540B-parameter language model with just eight chain of thought exemplars achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on the GSM8K benchmark of math word problems.
claims.evidence: For instance, prompting a 540B-parameter language model with just eight chain of thought exemplars achieves state of the art accuracy on the GSM8K benchmark of math word problems, surpassing even finetuned GPT-3 with a verifier.

methods.name: Chain of Thought Prompting
methods.description: A method where a few chain of thought demonstrations are provided as exemplars in prompting to improve complex reasoning in large language models.

assumptions.statement: Sufficiently large language models can naturally develop reasoning abilities when prompted with chain of thought exemplars.

limitations.statement: The effectiveness of chain of thought prompting may vary across different types of reasoning tasks and model sizes.

title: A Unifying Lens on Supervised Fine-Tuning Through Target Distribution Design

claims.statement: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can be more effective when the target distribution is designed to account for token uncertainty and model prior.
claims.evidence: TARGET-SFT, which constructs the training objective directly from the desired target distribution, consistently outperforms across the ten reasoning dataset-model settings evaluated.

claims.statement: The Q-target framework unifies many existing SFT variants by decomposing objective design into two explicit choices: how much to rely on the observed token and how to allocate the remaining probability mass.
claims.evidence: The Q-target framework reveals that many existing SFT variants can be understood as varying ways of answering these two questions, and seemingly different losses correspond to implicit choices of target distribution Q.

claims.statement: TARGET-SFT adaptively balances strict imitation and prior preservation, leading to better performance on reasoning tasks.
claims.evidence: TARGET-SFT consistently gives the best results across all models on both mathematical and medical reasoning tasks.

methods.name: Q-target framework

methods.name: TARGET-SFT

methods.name: Standard SFT
methods.description: A method that maximizes the likelihood of every token in a demonstrated trajectory using a one-hot target distribution.

title: UBP2: Uncertainty-Balanced Preference Planning for Efficient Preference-based Reinforcement Learning

claims.statement: UBP2 achieves higher sample efficiency than model-free preference-based methods and non-optimistic model-based baselines on the Meta-World benchmark.
claims.evidence: Empirically, experiments on the Meta-World benchmark show UBP2 achieves substantially higher sample efficiency than model-free preference-based methods and non-optimistic model-based baselines.

claims.statement: UBP2 uses ensembles of reward, dynamics, and value function models to evaluate candidate trajectories according to a unified score.
claims.evidence: Our method, Uncertainty-Balanced Preference Planning (UBP2), uses ensembles of reward, dynamics, and value function models to evaluate candidate trajectories according to a unified score that combines expected reward, terminal value, and epistemic uncertainty.

claims.statement: UBP2 establishes sublinear regret guarantees for both finite-horizon and infinite-horizon settings under standard regularity assumptions.
claims.evidence: Under standard regularity assumptions, we establish sublinear regret guarantees for both finite-horizon and infinite-horizon settings.

title: Reference-Driven Multi-Speaker Audio Scene Generation from In-the-Wild Priors

claims.statement: ScenA outperforms existing multi-speaker systems on speaker-binding metrics while generating rich conversational audio with overlapping speech, emotional vocalizations, and ambient sound.
claims.evidence: We evaluate ScenA on the CoVoMix2-Dialogue benchmark, showing that it outperforms existing multi-speaker systems on speaker-binding metrics while generating rich conversational audio with overlapping speech, emotional vocalizations, and ambient sound.

claims.statement: The Reference Shortcut is a critical obstacle in conditioning a text-to-audio flow-matching foundation model on multiple reference voices and a free-form natural language prompt.
claims.evidence: However, we identify a critical obstacle to this approach: the Reference Shortcut. During training under standard noise schedules, the model can identify the matching reference by acoustic similarity to the noisy target, bypassing the text prompt entirely.

claims.statement: A high-noise-biased timestep distribution addresses the Reference Shortcut by forcing the model to rely on the text prompt for speaker assignment.
claims.evidence: We address this with a high-noise-biased timestep distribution that forces the model to rely on the text prompt for speaker assignment.

methods.name: ScenA
methods.description: A method that conditions a text-to-audio flow-matching foundation model on multiple reference voices and a free-form natural language prompt to generate multi-speaker audio scenes.

methods.name: high-noise-biased timestep distribution
methods.description: A technique to address the Reference Shortcut by forcing the model to rely on the text prompt for speaker assignment.

assumptions.statement: The text-to-audio flow-matching foundation model is pretrained on large-scale in-the-wild data.
The model can generate natural, non-studio audio including background noise, room acoustics, overlapping dialogue, and spontaneous paralinguistic events.

limitations.statement: The model can identify the matching reference by acoustic similarity to the noisy target, bypassing the text prompt entirely, which is addressed by the high-noise-biased timestep distribution.
